numerical_failure.observed_behavior: isin called values.as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True (the default), silently truncating finer-resolution values when converting down (e.g. ns -> s), so values differing at sub-unit precision incorrectly matched and returned True.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Values that differ at nanosecond precision should not match; the reproducer should return [False] because the values differ at nanosecond precision. The fix casts both arrays up to the finer resolution via _ensure_matching_resos instead of lossy downcasting.
trigger_conditions: DatetimeArray or TimedeltaArray (dtype kind 'M' or 'm') calls isin with values of a different, finer resolution than self
self has coarser unit (e.g. 's') and values have finer unit (e.g. 'ns'), so values are converted down to self.unit with round_ok=True
values differ only at sub-unit precision

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64 (M8) and timedelta64 (m8) arrays, i.e. DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray
numerical_characteristics.precision: nanosecond versus coarser units such as s, ms, us; truncation occurs when converting finer-resolution values down to self's unit (e.g. ns to s)
category_specific_evidence: PR#64545 reproducer: dta = pd.array(pd.to_datetime(["2020-01-01"]).as_unit("s")) and vals = pd.array(pd.to_datetime(["2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000001"]).as_unit("ns")); dta.isin(vals) returns [True] before the fix (wrong) and [False] after (correct), since the values differ by 1 nanosecond at ns precision
Root cause per commit: isin called as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True (the default), silently truncating finer-resolution values when converting down (ns to s), so sub-unit differences matched
Fix: replace the lossy downcast with _ensure_matching_resos, which casts both arrays up to the finer resolution with no information loss

Added test test_isin_mismatched_reso parametrized over dtype_kind M and m and resolution pairs (s,ns), (ms,us), (us,ns), (ns,s); test arrays are [0, 1] and value [1] at the respective units, expected result for non-equal values is [False, False]
